description: Per-ticket cross-model adversarial review: an optional loop, configured in .redeye.json, where a review-role model reviews each ticket branch before merge and the implement-role model must fix or dispute each finding. Only the reviewer can close a finding. Source: tasks/prd-adversarial-review.md and .scratch/adversarial-review/spec.md. With no .redeye.json or no adversarial key, behavior is unchanged. Tests assert observable results (ticket Status, merged or not, branch exists, progress.md, review log contents, which role got which prompt, exit code), never prompt wording, log wording or internal call order.

userStories.title: Ticket review log format

userStories.title: One review step gates each ticket
userStories.description: As a redeye user, I want every ticket reviewed by the review model at least once before it is marked done, so that no ticket merges unchecked. (From ticket 04.)
acceptanceCriteria: In runTicketAttempt, after runTestGate passes and before the attempt reports ready to merge, a round runner in src/review.ts runs the review step in the ticket's worktree
The round runner takes spawnAgent and the process registry as injected deps, and imports only types from src/orchestrator.ts
The reviewer prompt is built from the ticket body, its spec, and the merge-base-to-head diff (minus .scratch/), and reuses CONFINEMENT_RULES and the read-only rules from src/rules.ts
The reviewer runs with the review role's provider and model; implementation runs with the implement role's
The reviewer process joins existing process tracking so the signal handler kills it
`No findings.` lets the ticket merge as today; the log has one round and a pass entry

A reviewer that exits non-zero, times out, or writes unparseable findings after its retries fails the attempt; the ticket gets done:false in progress.md and goes through the existing ticket retry policy
Until US-012 lands, open findings also fail the attempt
The ticket review log is committed with the other bookkeeping files at every terminal point (git add --force)
Every attempt that reaches the loop appends a terminal entry (pass, failed or unresolved) before it returns; the log is only appended to, never truncated
Round numbers restart at 1 for each attempt, and the reviewer is given only the current attempt's open findings

Integration test: a loop that fails (reviewer exits non-zero) and is retried logs a failed entry, then the retry's reviewer outputs `No findings.` and the ticket merges, with the retry's round recorded as round 1
With no adversarial key, agent invocations match today's and no reviewer is spawned
Integration tests in test/review-integration.test.ts use runWavesIsolated with the mock agents

userStories.title: Fix step with the implement role
userStories.description: As a redeye user, I want the implement model to fix or dispute each open finding and then pass the tests again, so that review findings turn into real changes. (From ticket 05.) A timed-out fixer follows the existing timeout invariant: it is not a failure. A timed-out reviewer is still a failure (US-011).
acceptanceCriteria: When findings are open and rounds remain, the implement role runs as the fixer in the ticket's worktree, using the existing runFixer contract: fix with /tdd and mark [x], or dispute by leaving the finding unchecked and writing the reason in its notes file
The fixer process joins existing process tracking
After the fix step, the test gate runs again in the worktree
On a test failure, the fixer runs again with the failure in its prompt (existing fix-retry); when those attempts run out, the attempt fails and the existing ticket retry policy applies
The round's log entry records the fixer's response to each finding, the test gate result, and the branch head after the fix

A fixer that times out is not a failure: its dirty changes are auto-committed, the test gate runs (with the existing fix-retry on failure), and if it passes the next round's review runs. Findings it did not address stay open for the reviewer
The fake agent can script fix, dispute, failing-tests and timeout behavior through new FAKE_* keys, added to the test file's key list
Integration test: a fixer whose changes keep failing the test gate fails the attempt, and the ticket goes through the retry path
Integration test: a fixer that times out with uncommitted changes has them committed on the ticket branch, the attempt does not fail, and a next review round is recorded in the log
